questions.question: Akshay invests a sum of ₹5400 and Atul invests a sum of ₹9400 at the same rate of simple interest per annum. If, at the end of 6 years, Atul gets ₹360 more interest than Akshay, then find the rate of interest per annum (in percentage).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The extra interest earned by Atul is due to his extra investment over the same time period.

Extra Principal = 9400 − 5400 = ₹4000

This extra ₹4000 yields an extra simple interest of ₹360 in 6 years.

Rate (R) = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T)

R = (360 × 100) ÷ (4000 × 6) = 36000 ÷ 24000 = 1.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 1.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Akshay's Principal, P₁ = ₹5400

Atul's Principal, P₂ = ₹9400

Time, T = 6 years

Difference in interest = ₹360

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 Investment & Extra Interest Analysis
 
 Akshay
 
 ₹5400
 
 Atul
 
 ₹5400
 
 
 + ₹4000
 
 
• 
 

 
 Yields ₹360 interest in 6 yrs

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI of Atul − SI of Akshay = 360

⇒ [(9400 × R × 6) ÷ 100] − [(5400 × R × 6) ÷ 100] = 360

⇒ 564R − 324R = 360

⇒ 240R = 360

⇒ R = 360 ÷ 240

⇒ R = 1.5

**∴ The correct answer is 1.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Formula

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where P is the Principal amount, R is the Rate of Interest, and T is the Time period in years.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

Simple Interest is calculated only on the initial principal amount. In contrast, Compound Interest is calculated on the principal as well as the accumulated interest of previous periods.

Difference Between SI and CI

For 2 years, the difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest on a certain principal at the same rate is derived using the formula: Difference = P(R ÷ 100)².

questions.question: Two trains having lengths of 410 m and 440 m are running at speeds of 60 km/h and 70 km/h, respectively, in the same direction. The time taken (in minutes) by the faster train, coming from behind, to completely cross the other train is:

Total distance to cross = Sum of train lengths = 410 + 440 = 850 m.

Relative speed (same direction) = 70 − 60 = 10 km/h.

Convert relative speed to m/s = 10 × (5/18) = 50/18 m/s.

Time in seconds = Distance ÷ Speed = 850 ÷ (50/18) = 850 × (18/50) = 306 seconds.

Time in minutes = 306 ÷ 60 = 5.1 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.1 minutes.**

questions.question: A shopkeeper bought an article for ₹500. At what price (in ₹) should he sell the article to make 22% profit?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost Price (CP) is always considered to be 100%.

Selling Price (SP) at 22% profit = 100% + 22% = 122% of CP.

SP = 122% of &rupee;500

SP = 122 × 5 = &rupee;610

**∴ The correct answer is &rupee;610.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = &rupee;500

Profit = 22%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

 
 CP = &rupee;500
 
 SP = &rupee;610
 

 + 22% Profit
 Profit = &rupee;110
 
 
 

 
 

**Calculation:**

⇒ SP = 500 × (100 + 22) ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 500 × 122 ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 5 × 122

⇒ SP = &rupee;610

**∴ The correct answer is &rupee;610.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Formula

When an article is sold at a loss, SP = CP × (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Successive Profit

If an article goes through multiple transactions with profits P₁% and P₂%, Net Profit% = P₁ + P₂ + (P₁ × P₂) ÷ 100.

questions.question: The LCM of two numbers is 105 and numbers are in ratio of 5 : 3, then the sum of the numbers is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the common multiplier be x, so the numbers are 5x and 3x.

LCM of 5x and 3x = 15x.

Given LCM = 105 ⇒ 15x = 105 ⇒ x = 7.

Sum of the numbers = 5x + 3x = 8x.

Sum = 8 × 7 = 56.

**∴ The correct answer is 56.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The ratio of the two numbers = 5 : 3

The LCM of the numbers = 105

 Ratio of Numbers: 5 : 3
 
 
 First Number = 5x
 
 
 Second = 3x

 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 

 

 Total Sum = 8x = 56
 
 LCM (5x, 3x) = 15x = 105 → x = 7

**Concept Used:**

If two numbers are in the ratio a : b, their LCM is a × b × HCF (provided a and b are co-prime).

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the numbers be 5x and 3x, where x is their HCF.

⇒ LCM of 5x and 3x = 15x

⇒ We are given that the LCM is 105.

⇒ 15x = 105

⇒ x = 105 ÷ 15 = 7

⇒ First number = 5 × 7 = 35

⇒ Second number = 3 × 7 = 21

⇒ Sum of the numbers = 35 + 21 = 56

**∴ The correct answer is 56.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM and Ratio Rule

If two numbers are in the ratio a : b (where a and b are co-prime), their LCM is equal to a × b × HCF. The numbers themselves are a × HCF and b × HCF.

Product of Two Numbers

For any two numbers, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM. Formula: N₁ × N₂ = HCF × LCM.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be co-prime if their Highest Common Factor (HCF) is 1. The LCM of two co-prime numbers is simply their product.
</p

questions.question: Pinki, Chinki and Reema started a work and Reema left after 4 days when 46% of the work is completed and then work got completed in 9 more days. In how many days can Reema alone complete the work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Total Work = 100%.

Combined efficiency of (Pinki + Chinki + Reema) = 46% ÷ 4 days = 11.5% per day.

Combined efficiency of (Pinki + Chinki) = (100% − 46%) ÷ 9 days = 54% ÷ 9 = 6% per day.

Reema's efficiency = 11.5% − 6% = 5.5% per day.

Time taken by Reema alone = 100% ÷ 5.5% = 1000 ÷ 55 = 200/11 = 18²/₁₁ days.

**∴ The correct answer is 18²/₁₁ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Let the total work be 100 units.

⇒ Work completed by Pinki, Chinki and Reema in 4 days = 46% of 100 = 46 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 100 − 46 = 54 units.

⇒ Pinki and Chinki completed the remaining 54 units in 9 days.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of (Pinki + Chinki + Reema) = 46 ÷ 4 = 11.5 units/day.

⇒ Days required by them for full work = 100 ÷ 11.5 = 200/23 days.

⇒ Efficiency of (Pinki + Chinki) = 54 ÷ 9 = 6 units/day.

⇒ Days required by them for full work = 100 ÷ 6 = 50/3 days.

 
 

 **Person**

 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**

⇒ Efficiency of Reema = Efficiency of (Pinki + Chinki + Reema) − Efficiency of (Pinki + Chinki)

⇒ Efficiency of Reema = 11.5 − 6 = 5.5 units/day.

⇒ Time taken by Reema alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 100 ÷ 5.5 = 1000/55 = 200/11 days.

⇒ 200 ÷ 11 = 18 with a remainder of 2 = 18²/₁₁ days.

**∴ The correct answer is 18²/₁₁ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Work and Efficiency

Total work is considered as the LCM of the days taken by individuals. Efficiency is inversely proportional to time: Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time Taken.

Persons Leaving Mid-way

When a person leaves before completing the work, calculate the work done by them during their active days. Subtract this from the total work, and the remaining work is divided by the efficiency of the remaining workers.

Percentage Based Work

When total work is given in percentages instead of days, always assume Total Work = 100% or 100 units to bypass complex fractional calculations.
</p

**Calculations:**

⇒ x = 460 ÷ 4

⇒ x = 115

⇒ Number of female employees = 3x

Ratio vs Proportion

A ratio compares two quantities of the same kind, while proportion is an equation stating that two ratios are equal (a : b = c : d).

Inverse Ratio

Duplicate & Triplicate Ratio

For a given ratio a : b, the duplicate ratio is a² : b² and the triplicate ratio is a³ : b³.

questions.question: Anand has ₹1218 with him. He divided it amongst his sons Anil and Ashok and asked them to invest it at 10% rate of interest compounded annually. It was seen that Anil and Ashok got same amount after 15 and 16 years respectively. How much (in ₹) did Anand give to Ashok?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When amounts are equal under compound interest, the ratio of shares is based on the compounding factor raised to the difference in time.

Difference in time = 16 − 15 = 1 year.

Multiplying factor for 10% = 1 + 10/100 = 11/10.

Ratio of initial shares (Anil : Ashok) = 11 : 10.

Ashok's share = 10 / (11 + 10) × 1218 = 10/21 × 1218 = ₹580.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹580.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total amount to be divided = ₹1218

Rate of compound interest (R) = 10% per annum

Time for Anil's investment = 15 years

Time for Ashok's investment = 16 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)T

 
 Total: ₹1218

 
• 
 
• 

 
 Anil's Share
 T = 15 yrs

 
 Ashok's Share
 T = 16 yrs

 
• 
 
• 

 
 Equal Amount

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the share of Anil be x and the share of Ashok be y.

⇒ x + y = 1218

⇒ According to the question, the amount received by both will be equal.

⇒ x(1 + 10/100)¹⁵ = y(1 + 10/100)¹⁶

⇒ x(11/10)¹⁵ = y(11/10)¹⁶

⇒ x = y(11/10)¹⁶ − ¹⁵

⇒ x = y(11/10)

⇒ x/y = 11/10

⇒ Ratio of shares of Anil and Ashok = 11 : 10

⇒ Sum of ratio parts = 11 + 10 = 21 parts

⇒ 21 parts = 1218

⇒ 1 part = 1218 ÷ 21 = 58

⇒ Ashok's share (y) = 10 parts = 10 × 58 = 580

**∴ The correct answer is ₹580.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Equal Amounts in Compound Interest

When a sum is divided into two parts P₁ and P₂ invested at r% for t₁ and t₂ years respectively such that their accumulated amounts are equal, the initial sums are in the ratio P₁ / P₂ = (1 + r/100)t² − t¹.

Effective Compound Multiplier

For a 10% rate of interest, the fractional multiplier is 11/10 or 1.1 per year. This means the total sum grows by 1.1 times its previous year's value every successive compounding cycle.

Sum Distribution based on Ratios

If a total amount T is to be divided in the ratio a : b, the individual respective shares are calculated as a / (a + b) × T and b / (a + b) × T.

questions.question: The price (per litre) of petrol increases by 75%. By what percent should its consumption be reduced such that the expenditure on it increases by 26% only?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let initial expenditure be 100.

If consumption is constant, new expenditure due to 75% price hike = 175.

However, the required new expenditure is 126 (as a 26% increase is allowed).

Reduction required in consumption = (175 − 126) ÷ 175 × 100

⇒ Reduction % = (49 ÷ 175) × 100 = 28%

**∴ The correct answer is 28%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Price increase = 75%

Expenditure increase = 26%

**Formula Used:**

Expenditure = Price × Consumption

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 
 Base: 100
 

 +75% (Price)
 

 +26% (Exp)
 
 175
 
 126
 

 Reduction
 Reduction % = (175 − 126) ÷ 175 × 100 = 28%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let original price be 100 and original consumption be 100.

⇒ Original Expenditure = 100 × 100 = 10000

⇒ New Price = 100 + 75 = 175

⇒ New Expenditure = 10000 × (100 + 26) ÷ 100 = 12600

⇒ Let new consumption be C.

⇒ 175 × C = 12600

⇒ C = 12600 ÷ 175 = 72

⇒ Reduction in consumption = 100 − 72 = 28

⇒ Reduction percentage = (28 ÷ 100) × 100 = 28%

**∴ The correct answer is 28%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product Constancy Rule

If the price of a commodity increases by a% and expenditure remains unchanged, consumption must decrease by (a ÷ (100 + a)) × 100%.

Successive Percentage Change

When Price and Consumption both change, the net effect on Expenditure is calculated using the formula: a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100.

Ratio Method

Consumption Ratio = Expenditure Ratio ÷ Price Ratio. This enables solving complex percentage fractions easily by converting them into equivalent simplified ratios.
</p

questions.question: Bipin offers a discount scheme that on buying 7 notebooks, get 3 for free. What will be the sale price (in ₹) of a notebook with a marked price ₹185, if the equivalent percentage discount is applied?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a Buy X Get Y Free scheme, Discount % = Free Items ÷ Total Items × 100

Equivalent Discount % = 3 ÷ (7 + 3) × 100 = 30%

Sale Price = (100% − 30%) of Marked Price

Sale Price = 0.70 × 185 = 129.50

**∴ The correct answer is ₹129.50.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 

 Total = 10 Notebooks
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 7 Paid Notebooks
 
 

 3 Free Notebooks
 
 
 Equivalent Discount = (3 ÷ 10) × 100 = 30%

**Given:**

⇒ Free items = 3

⇒ Paid items = 7

⇒ Marked Price (MP) of 1 notebook = ₹185

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Equivalent Discount % = [Free items ÷ (Paid items + Free items)] × 100

⇒ Sale Price (SP) = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Equivalent Discount % = [3 ÷ (7 + 3)] × 100

⇒ Equivalent Discount % = (3 ÷ 10) × 100 = 30%

⇒ Sale Price of 1 notebook = 185 × (100 − 30) ÷ 100

⇒ Sale Price = 185 × (70 ÷ 100)

⇒ Sale Price = 185 × 0.7

⇒ Sale Price = 129.50

**∴ The correct answer is ₹129.50.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Buy X Get Y Free

The effective discount is always calculated on the total number of items received (X + Y), not just the paid items. Discount % = Y ÷ (X + Y) × 100.

Successive Discounts

When multiple discounts are given sequentially (e.g., a% and b%), the effective single discount is calculated as: D = a + b − (a × b ÷ 100).

Marked Price & Selling Price Relation

Selling Price (SP) is obtained after deducting the discount from Marked Price (MP). SP = MP − Discount = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

questions.question: In a circular race track of 1500 meters, runners A and B start simultaneously from the same point in the same direction. If A runs at 45 km/h and B runs at 36 km/h, after how much time will A meet B for the first time?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed (same direction) = 45 − 36 = 9 km/h

Convert to m/min: 9 × (1000 ÷ 60) = 150 m/min

Time to meet = Track Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Time = 1500 ÷ 150 = 10 min

**∴ The correct answer is 10 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the circular track = 1500 m

Speed of runner A = 45 km/h

Speed of runner B = 36 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Time to meet (same direction) = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

 
 
 Track = 1500 m
 
 Start Point
 

 

 A: 45 km/h
 B: 36 km/h
 Relative Speed = 45 − 36 = 9 km/h
 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative speed = Speed of A − Speed of B

⇒ Relative speed = 45 − 36 = 9 km/h

⇒ Convert km/h to m/min = 9 × (1000 ÷ 60) = 150 m/min

⇒ Total distance to cover to meet first time = 1500 m

⇒ Time taken = Distance ÷ Relative speed

⇒ Time taken = 1500 ÷ 150 = 10 min

**∴ The correct answer is 10 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Meeting Anywhere (Same Direction)

When two bodies run around a circular track in the same direction, they meet for the first time after: Time = Distance ÷ (S₁ − S₂).

Meeting Anywhere (Opposite Direction)

When two bodies run around a circular track in opposite directions, they meet for the first time after: Time = Distance ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Meeting at Starting Point

The time taken to meet for the first time exactly at the starting point is the LCM of the times taken by each to complete one round: Time = LCM(T₁, T₂).
</p

questions.question: The price of a mobile phone was Rs. 18,000 last year. It has increased by 15.75% next year, what is the value of new price?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Break down the 15.75% increase into components: 10% + 5% + 0.75%.

10% = 1,800 | 5% = 900 | 0.75% = (3 ÷ 4) of 1% = 135

Total increase = 1,800 + 900 + 135 = 2,835

New Price = Original Price + Increase = 18,000 + 2,835 = 20,835

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 20,835.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Original Price = Rs. 18,000

Percentage Increase = 15.75%

 
 
 Base Price: 18,000
 + 15.75%
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 New Price = 20,835

**Formula Used:**

New Value = Original Value × (1 + Percentage Increase ÷ 100)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Increase = 15.75% of 18,000

⇒ Increase = (15.75 ÷ 100) × 18,000

⇒ Increase = 15.75 × 180

⇒ Increase = 2,835

⇒ New Price = 18,000 + 2,835 = 20,835

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 20,835.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage change is always determined with respect to the initial value: [(New Value − Old Value) ÷ Old Value] × 100.

Successive Percentage Change

If a value changes by a% and then further changes by b%, the net percentage change is given by the formula: a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100.

Concept of Base in Percentage

In all percentage calculations, the reference point from which the change occurs represents the 100% base value.
</p

questions.question: 400 oranges were bought at ₹1250 per hundred and were sold at a profit of ₹1000. Find the selling price (in ₹) per dozen of oranges.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost price (CP) of 400 oranges = 4 × ₹1250 = ₹5000

Total Selling Price (SP) = CP + Profit = ₹5000 + ₹1000 = ₹6000

Selling price of 1 orange = ₹6000 ÷ 400 = ₹15

Selling price per dozen (12 oranges) = ₹15 × 12 = ₹180

**∴ The correct answer is ₹180.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of oranges bought = 400

Cost price per 100 oranges = ₹1250

Total profit earned = ₹1000

**Formula Used:**

Total CP = (CP per 100) × (Total quantity ÷ 100)

Total SP = Total CP + Profit

SP of 1 dozen = (Total SP ÷ Total quantity) × 12

 
 
 Total CP = ₹5000
 
 
 
 Profit = ₹1000
 
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 Total SP = ₹6000 (400 oranges)
 
 
 SP per dozen = (₹6000 ÷ 400) × 12 = ₹180
 
 
 Profit & Loss Analysis

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total CP of 400 oranges = ₹1250 × (400 ÷ 100) = ₹5000

⇒ Total SP = ₹5000 + ₹1000 = ₹6000

⇒ Selling price of 1 orange = ₹6000 ÷ 400 = ₹15

⇒ Selling price of one dozen (12 oranges) = ₹15 × 12 = ₹180

**∴ The correct answer is ₹180.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit occurs when the Selling Price (SP) is greater than the Cost Price (CP). The formula to find the profit amount is Profit = SP − CP.

Profit Percentage

Profit % is always calculated based on the Cost Price unless specified otherwise. Formula: Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Unitary Method

This method involves finding the value of a single unit directly and then multiplying it by the desired quantity to find the final value.

questions.question: The LCM of 26, 34, 221 and 195 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Factorize mentally by extracting visible prime factors like 13 and 17.

26 = 13 × 2, 34 = 17 × 2, 221 = 13 × 17, 195 = 13 × 3 × 5

Pick the highest power of all distinct primes involved: 2, 3, 5, 13, and 17.

LCM = 2 × 3 × 5 × 13 × 17 = 6630.

**∴ The correct answer is 6630.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are 26, 34, 221, and 195.

**Concept Used:**

The Least Common Multiple (LCM) is the product of the highest powers of all prime factors found in the given numbers.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 26 = 2 × 13

⇒ Prime factorization of 34 = 2 × 17

⇒ Prime factorization of 221 = 13 × 17

⇒ Prime factorization of 195 = 3 × 5 × 13

⇒ Identifying all prime factors: 2, 3, 5, 13, and 17.

⇒ The maximum power of each prime factor present in any factorization is 1.

⇒ LCM = 2¹ × 3¹ × 5¹ × 13¹ × 17¹

⇒ LCM = (2 × 5) × 3 × (13 × 17)

⇒ LCM = 10 × 3 × 221

⇒ LCM = 30 × 221 = 6630

**∴ The correct answer is 6630.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The largest integer that divides all given numbers without leaving a remainder. It is calculated as the product of the lowest powers of all common prime factors.

Product Rule for Two Numbers

For any two numbers A and B, the product of the numbers is strictly equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: A × B = HCF(A, B) × LCM(A, B).

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are considered co-prime if their Highest Common Factor (HCF) is exactly 1. The LCM of two co-prime numbers will always be equal to their direct product.
</p

questions.question: Find the fourth proportional to 20, 24 and 30.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For finding the fourth proportional x to the numbers a, b, and c: Product of Extremes = Product of Means

⇒ 20 × x = 24 × 30

⇒ 20x = 720

⇒ x = 36

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First term (a) = 20

Second term (b) = 24

Third term (c) = 30

Let the fourth proportional be x.

**Formula Used:**

If four quantities are in proportion (a : b :: c : d), the product of the extreme terms is equal to the product of the mean terms.

⇒ a × d = b × c

 

 Product of Extremes (20 × x)

 

 Product of Means (24 × 30)

 
 20
 1st

 :

 
 24
 2nd

 ::

 
 30
 3rd

 :

 
 x
 4th

**Calculations:**

⇒ 20 × x = 24 × 30

⇒ 20x = 720

⇒ x = 720 ÷ 20

⇒ x = 36

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fourth Proportional

If four numbers a, b, c, and d are in proportion (a : b :: c : d), then d is called the fourth proportional to a, b, and c. It is found using the relation d = (b × c) ÷ a.

Third Proportional

If three numbers a, b, and c are in a continued proportion (a : b = b : c), then c is considered the third proportional. It is calculated using the formula c = b² ÷ a.

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional (or geometric mean) between two given numbers a and b is the square root of their product. The direct formula is Mean Proportional = √(a × b).

Componendo & Dividendo Rule

When two fractions are proportional, a / b = c / d, applying the componendo and dividendo property yields the equation (a + b) / (a − b) = (c + d) / (c − d).
</p
